what: Real string players' level at pp / mf / ff measured from fixed-gain recordings, and the SSO string section balance it implies at each MuseScore dynamic (pp p mp mf f ff), against the fixed balance M (Vn1 -3.81, Vn2 -2.66, Va -2.12, Vc +2.77, Cb +5.81). Research only (2026-10-11): no playback change.
made_by: tools/soundlibraries/real_string_dynamics.py measure + analyze (python3 -P -E; numpy, soundfile, librosa 1.0.0 YIN, pyloudnorm 0.2.0)

iowaPre2011.what: University of Iowa Musical Instrument Samples, pre-2011 strings: Violin, Viola, Cello, Double Bass, arco, pp / mf / ff chromatic scales note by note, mono 16 bit 44.1 kHz, one Neumann KM 84, anechoic chamber (Wendell Johnson Speech and Hearing Center). 143 files, 676 MB.
iowaPre2011.licence: "may be downloaded and used for any projects, without restrictions" (MIS.html, read 2026-10-11). Only derived numbers are kept here; no audio in git.
iowaPre2011.fixedGain: MIS.html, of the recordings until 2011: "Because the recordings represent the complete dynamic structure of the instrument, input volume levels were not changed during the recording session." Checked here (gainCheck): cello and double bass, the 4-16 kHz noise between notes is the same at pp / mf / ff within 0.06-0.51 dB on every string, at -89.4 to -92.2 dB, 7-10 dB above the 16-bit TPDF dither floor in that band (-99.0 dB, computed with the same function in the test): a gain change would move it. Violin and viola: the gaps were edited to near digital silence (no 0.1 s block without exact zeros), so unchecked; the statement stands alone.

iowa2012.what: Iowa MIS strings recorded December 2011 - May 2012 (MISPost2012Intro.html), the centre microphone of three Earthworks QTC-40 downsampled to 16 bit 44.1 kHz mono (MIS.html); other players. 129 files, 922 MB. The post-2012 edited files were normalized to -0.4 dB (MISPost2012Intro.html step 11) and are not used.
iowa2012.fixedGain: not stated for these. Checked (gainCheck2012): viola 4-16 kHz gap noise within 0.04-0.12 dB over pp / mf / ff on every string (-94.1 dB, 5 dB above the dither floor): fixed. Double bass: no 4-16 kHz blocks, broadband gap noise within 0.68-3.09 dB per string: fixed within about 3 dB at worst, weaker evidence. Violin (4-16 kHz gap noise moves 22.6-47.9 dB, pp notes barely above a -49 dB noise) and cello (broadband gap noise moves up to 8.9 dB) fail and are not used for level. Many file names do not match the notes (e.g. Viola.arco.sulA.mf.C5B5 holds Bb3-A4) and YIN pitches are unreliable, so these players enter as pitch-agnostic session spans only (players2012).

weinzierl2018.what: Weinzierl, Lepa, Schultz, Detzner, von Coler, Behler (2018), "Sound power and timbre as cues for the dynamic strength of orchestral instruments", JASA 144(3) 1347-1355, doi 10.1121/1.5053113: single-note sound power at pp ("as soft as possible") and ff ("as loud as possible"), Table I. Per-note values: database version 3, 3_Audio_Features.csv, column SoundPower in dB, _et_ files, modern instruments (doi 10.14279/depositonce-5861.3).
weinzierl2018.licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (0_Documentation.pdf of the database, lines "The database is provided under a Creative Commons BY-NC-SA licence"): derived numbers only.

sources.clarkLuce1965: Clark & Luce (1965), "Intensities of orchestral instrument scales played at prescribed dynamic markings", JAES 13(2) 151-157: abstract only (secondary, via the 2026-10-11 literature search): average pp -> ff range about 11 dB for non-percussive instruments.
sources.sso: sso_cc1_curves.json (branch sso-cc1-curves, commit 329681d3a2, md5 7787c2044af6fb89a73c63d2532f96f9): SSO All techniques Long at CC1 16-127 every 3 semitones, measured 2026-10-11 on the Windows VM with the real library (Kontakt Player 8.13.1), median of 4 repeats.
sources.museScoreLevels: libmscore/ms4playback.cpp: ordinaryLevel pp 3750 p 4250 mp 4750 mf 5250 f 5750 ff 6250; expressionLevel -> CC1 32 48 64 80 96 112.

method: Notes: 50 ms level above the file's noise floor + 10 dB and within 40 dB of its loudest, >= 0.5 s (2012: >= 2.0 s, its gaps hold noise bursts); gaps < 0.3 s bridged. Pitch: YIN (librosa) median over the note's middle half, within the file name's range +- 1 semitone (pre-2011; 67 of 143 files hold another number of notes than the name says, and some pitches sit between semitones, e.g. Cello.arco.pp.sulC.C2Gb2: 12 notes 65.7-91.2 Hz), the instrument's range (2012).

Measures as the SSO side (sso_cc1_sweep.py): loudDb = loudest 50 ms (25 ms hop) of the note and 0.5 s after; rmsDb = mean power 1.5-3.0 s after the onset, or the middle half of notes shorter than 3.0 s (many Iowa notes last 1.5-2.5 s: a choice); lufs = BS.1770-4 integrated (pyloudnorm 0.2.0). Notes under 20 dB SNR left out (a choice; 10 and 30 dB in changePpToFfOtherSnr).

Spans: per string (one recording session, one gain) each dynamic linear in dB between its notes, on the semitones all three dynamics cover; pp->mf and mf->ff per semitone, averaged over strings. Absolute levels are never compared across sessions or instruments.

Real side of the balance: one player's level at MuseScore level L piecewise linear in dB through the measured pp (3750), mf (5250), ff (6250) (p, mp between pp and mf; f between mf and ff: a choice), anchored to Weinzierl's sound power at ff (main: both are a player's loudest single notes, while Iowa's pp spans only 25-65 % of Weinzierl's "as soft as possible"), at pp, or at the pp-ff midpoint (variants); section = player + 10 log10 N (16/14/12/10/8). Outside Iowa's semitones the nearest span (balanceWithinIowaRange restricts instead).

Balance as M (m_final.py): per section D = mean over M's pitch range of SSO(p, CC1 of the dynamic) - real section(p, dynamic); offset = -(D - mean of the five D). Anchor "wlinear" is the M / M_dyn model (Weinzierl alone, linear between pp and ff): at mp it reproduces M exactly (mpWeinzierlLinearMinusFixedM = 0).

Uncertainty: bootstrapChangePpToFf resamples each instrument's span semitones (understates: neighbours share notes); acrossStringsSdPpFf = SD of the pp->ff span between strings at one pitch (same player, other session); players2012 = a second viola and double bass player; three measures; SNR 10 / 30.

Not used: TU Berlin anechoic Beethoven 8 (Boehm, Ackermann, Weinzierl 2020, CC BY 4.0): in-context dynamics of real section players, but period instruments, the open excerpt is 0.6-0.7 GB per movement (disk had < 3 GB free) and it needs score-to-audio alignment; the next source to try.

summary.note: main result: pre-2011 Iowa players, per-semitone spans, loudDb, anchored at Weinzierl ff; dB to add to each section, centred over the five
